about.title: King City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: King City sits along a network of roads that carry both local traffic and travelers passing through Monterey County, and recent public records show 21 injury collisions in a single year, with 27 people hurt. Corridors like San Antonio Drive, S 1st Street, Broadway Street, and Ellis Street see a steady share of these incidents, and crash reports tend to cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., when work traffic and weekend errands overlap. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the days right after matter. Insurance adjusters often move quickly, sometimes asking for a recorded statement before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect injured people in King City with an independent attorney who can review the details, help preserve evidence like photos and witness contact information, and explain your options. There's no cost to get connected, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why King City Residents Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Time Limits Move Faster Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim, but if a government vehicle or road defect is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Talking with an attorney early helps make sure a King City claim doesn't get filed too late.

items.title: Fault Can Be Shared, Not All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for a crash on Broadway Street or elsewhere in town. An independent attorney can help make sure your share of fault is assessed fairly, not inflated by the other side's insurer.

items.title: No Cap on What You've Genuinely Lost
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront fee. You only owe attorney fees if there's a recovery, which keeps the process accessible after an unexpected injury.

items.question: Do I have to give a statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: No, you're not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it's often wise to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early recorded statements to minimize what they owe. An independent attorney can help you understand what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in King City?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If the collision involved a public road defect or a government-owned vehicle, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What should I do right after a crash on a busy road like San Antonio Drive?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of the vehicles, the road, and any visible injuries, and get contact information from witnesses before they leave. Seek medical attention even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms show up later. Once you're safe, connecting with an independent attorney can help you understand your next steps.
